item.title: 'I will not blink': Eisenkot sends stern message amid coalition deadlock
item.description: Yashar leader says coalition talks cannot continue indefinitely, sharply criticizes Netanyahu and warns against missing a chance to replace the government. If talks on a broad government fail, he plans to form a national emergency government.

item.title: Unusual moment on Lebanese TV: Christian commentator wears Jewish kippah
item.description: During a live Lebanese TV broadcast, Christian commentator Charles Jabbour wears a kippah bearing a Star of David and the name of the Israeli series Fauda.

item.title: Yisrael Beytenu MK rules out government with Arabs
item.description:
Amid efforts to form a government with the support of the Arab parties, MK Sharon Sharabi (Yisrael Beytenu) made clear that he would not support such a move.
"I stand by my promise and will continue to uphold it: I will not be part of a coalition that relies on supporters of terrorism, whether from within or from outside. Some principles are non-negotiable, and some values cannot be compromised," he declared.

item.title: Eisenkot: 'I won't drag things out. At right time, I'll present a new, good government for approval'
item.description:
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot announced that if efforts to form a broad government fail, he will move to establish a national emergency government.
"This is not a threat for negotiating purposes. It is a decision I have made based on my understanding of the responsibility and duties entrusted to me at this time of emergency," he said.
Eisenkot added that he intends to present a new government to the Knesset for approval at the appropriate time.

item.title: Officers from Moroccan Army arrive to partake in Gaza stabilization force
item.description: Additional officers from the Royal Moroccan Army have arrived to participate in the International Stabilization Force in Gaza. According to the ISF, the officers will add capacity to medical operations and logistics planning.

item.title: Security forces seize 15 drones in Judea and Samaria
item.description:
IDF, Border Police, and Judea and Samaria District Police forces confiscated approximately 15 drones across Judea and Samaria over the past week as part of a targeted operation to prevent the use of drones for terrorist purposes, including carrying and dropping explosives.
According to the IDF Spokesperson's Unit, more than 500 drones have been confiscated in the area since the beginning of 2026.
The IDF noted that the possession and operation of drones are prohibited in the area under an order issued by the IDF Central Command chief, and that efforts to counter the threat are ongoing.

item.title: Houthis: Saudi airspace to be target of operations in coming hours
item.description: The Houthi terrorist rebels in Yemen have issued a statement warning aviation companies that Saudi airspace is unsafe, as it will become a theater for their operations in the coming hours. The terror group noted that "the sacred airspace over Mecca and Medina" is not included in the warning.

item.title: Netanyahu warns against minority government: "This must stop immediately"
item.description: The PM said he recently briefed Liberman, Bennett and Eisenkot on security and urged a unity government. He opposed a minority government backed by Arab parties, "It's inconceivable. Every hour we wait is an hour wasted".

item.title: National consolidation
item.description: The struggles within Yaakov's young family are mirrrored in our young state's history. With maturity, come the recognition and understanding that we must live together, despite differences of opinion and roles.

item.title: Netanyahu: "We are at a historic crossroads, responsibility means unity"
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu addressed the security and political situation, saying: "We are at a historic crossroads. I briefed Lieberman and Eisenkot on the security situation. Responsibility means unity."
Netanyahu also addressed the possibility of forming a minority government, saying: "I hear that there is an intention to swear in a minority government as early as the beginning of next week. It is inconceivable."

item.title: Dutch Jews increasingly afraid to display Jewish identity amid rising antisemitism
item.description: Doron Sanders, president of the Mizrachi movement in the Netherlands, tells Arutz Sheva that growing antisemitism is prompting some Jews to conceal their identity, while others are considering immigrating to Israel.
